years_since_diagnosis.evidence: been dealing with Crohn's disease for almost 15 years now

occupation.evidence: starting my first real job as a teacher

location.evidence: GI doctor ordered a colonoscopy and showed cobblestone road images of intestines; colonoscopy primarily visualizes colon, and cobblestone appearance is classic colonic Crohn's, though small bowel involvement not ruled out

severity.evidence: Multiple biologic failures, hospitalization with partial bowel obstruction, ongoing frequent symptoms despite Stelara, debilitating fatigue, long treatment history including multiple biologics

disease_control.evidence: Still have frequent symptoms but avoiding surgery. That's the goal now - avoid surgery as long as possible.

treatments.reason_stopped: Side effects (weight gain, insomnia, mood swings); used as induction only
treatments.evidence: Started on prednisone and mesalamine right away. The prednisone was horrible - gained 30 pounds, couldn't sleep, mood swings that scared me. But it did calm the inflammation.

treatments.reason_stopped: Flaring again within three months on mesalamine alone
treatments.evidence: Tried to maintain on just mesalamine but within three months I was flaring again.

treatments.reason_stopped: Developed severe joint pain; stopped due to possible drug-induced arthritis
treatments.evidence: Added azathioprine. Worked for about a year until I developed severe joint pain... had to stop the medication.

treatments.reason_stopped: Secondary loss of response during second pregnancy
treatments.evidence: Started Remicade when I was 24... Remicade worked wonderfully for about four years... Then during my second pregnancy, it stopped working.
After delivery, started Humira... Humira worked for three years... When Humira failed...

treatments.reason_stopped: Insurance denied three times; never actually started
treatments.evidence: tried Cimzia. Insurance denied it three times.
Finally got approved for Stelara. Been on it two years. It's okay, not great. Still have frequent symptoms but avoiding surgery.
Doctor mentioned combination therapy next - adding methotrexate to Stelara.

encounters.evidence: When I finally saw a doctor, she said IBS and gave me fiber supplements.

After six months of increasing pain and weight loss, I demanded a referral to a specialist. The GI doctor ordered a colonoscopy immediately... That's when we moved to biologics. Started Remicade when I was 24.
Rheumatologist couldn't determine if it was drug-induced or Crohn's-related arthritis.
While fighting insurance, ended up hospitalized with partial bowel obstruction.

status.evidence: Finally got approved for Stelara. Been on it two years.

barriers.evidence: Multiple prior biologics (Remicade, Humira) required before Stelara; Cimzia denied three times by insurance before Stelara approved
Insurance denied Cimzia three times. Finally got approved for Stelara.

referral_steps_gp_to_prescriber.evidence: GP (step 1) -> GI specialist who prescribed biologics (step 2)

extraction_notes: Patient is currently on Stelara (biologic, status=on). Cimzia was denied by insurance and never started — listed as not_started. Methotrexate is planned as add-on combination therapy, not yet started. B12 injections, vitamin D, iron infusions are supplements/supportive care for deficiencies, not IBD treatments — excluded from treatments list. Chronic migraine and fibromyalgia are comorbidities. Rheumatologist visit was a side consult (not on referral path). Hospitalization for bowel obstruction was not a new referral step leading to a new provider. Disease location inferred as colonic from colonoscopy/cobblestone description but small bowel involvement cannot be excluded. Transcript ends with a complete, settled thought ('Kids need me') — completeness=complete.
